newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam says Iran still holds Iraqi POWs.
newsitem.headline: Saddam says Iran still holds Iraqi POWs.

text.p: President Saddam Hussein on Friday marked the anniversary of the end of the 1980-1988 Iraq-Iran war by demanding Iran's new president frees Iraqi prisoners of war .

In a speech carried live by Iraqi media, Saddam said it was against the principles of Islam to "murder and mutilate bodies of (Iraqi) prisoners of war after each battle (with Iran) and to keep in captivity others for 17 years...."
Iran denies it still holds Iraqi POW's.

Saddam urged new Iranian President Mohammad Khatami to fulfill Iran's commitements toward Iraq by releasing Iraqi POWs and handing back several civilian and military planes which Baghdad sent to Iran at the start of the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait to escape bombing.
"Other than that we will still not be content to see Iran merely changing posts and replacing an individual or a party with another," Saddam said.
The Iraqi leader blamed the instability in Iraq's south, which started soon after the ceasefire of the 1991 Gulf War , on Iran.
"At that time they pushed the most evil people...to burn and to destroy everything that was not reached by bombs of the 30- state aggression," Saddam said.
He said the Iranian rulers tried to push Iraq into an earlier confrontation with the U.S.-led allies in 1991 in order not to "lose the opportunity of betrayal."
